core_obligations: Additivity and the zero object (proof lines 4941-4944): the direct sum of two filtered objects is the direct sum of the underlying objects with the filtration given componentwise, which makes the category additive, and the zero object is displayed with its filtration.

Kernels, cokernels, images and coimages (proof lines 4945-4949): the kernel of a morphism of filtered objects is the inclusion of the kernel endowed with the induced filtration and the cokernel is the quotient map onto the cokernel endowed with the quotient filtration; since these exist, so do all images and coimages.
Non-abelianness (proof lines 4950-4952): the cited example shows that the category is not abelian in general.
proof_roadmap: Compute the direct sum and the zero object with their filtrations.
Describe the kernel via the induced filtration and the cokernel via the quotient filtration.
Cite the example witnessing failure of abelianness.
difficulty_reason: The lemma lists the categorical properties of the category of filtered objects of an abelian category: it is additive, has a zero object, has kernels, cokernels, images and coimages, but is not abelian in general (statement lines 4927-4938). The proof is a complete argument: the direct sum with its componentwise filtration gives additivity (proof lines 4941-4944); the kernel with the induced filtration and the cokernel with the quotient filtration are exhibited, which also provides images and coimages (proof lines 4945-4949); and the failure of abelianness is delegated to a named example (proof lines 4950-4952). The non-formal content is the identification of the kernels and cokernels with the induced and quotient filtrations. The claim is H2: a structured argument with each input named.
